quotes.quote: specifically designed to evaluate the physical reasoning abilities of (M)LLMs on real-world Physics Olympiads from 2024–2025
Up-to-date Coverage : Includes 13 Olympiad exam papers from 2024–2025 across international and regional competitions.
New (Dec. 19): Results from GPT-5.2 (high) have been added to the HiPhO Leaderboard.

New (Dec. 8): Results from Gemini-3-Pro, DeepSeek-V3.2-Speciale, and Kimi-K2-Thinking have been added to the HiPhO Leaderboard. Notably, Gemini-3-Pro achieved gold-medal performance across all 13 Olympiads in HiPhO.
New (Nov. 5): We added CPhO 2025 (Chinese Physics Olympiad) — the national final theoretical exam to the HiPhO benchmark.
New (Sep. 16): We launched "PhyArena", a physics reasoning leaderboard incorporating the HiPhO benchmark.
Contact: fangchenyu@link.cuhk.edu.cn
Closed-source reasoning MLLMs lead the benchmark, earning 6–12 gold medals (Top 5: Gemini-2.5-Pro, Gemini-2.5-Flash-Thinking, GPT-5, o3, Grok-4)
Open-source LLMs demonstrate stronger reasoning and generally outperform open-source MLLMs
13 Physics Olympiads
5 Physics Fields: Mechanics, Electromagnetism, Thermodynamics, Optics, Modern Physics
4 Modality Types: Text-Only, Text+Illustration Figure, Text+Variable Figure, Text+Data Figure
6 Answer Types: Expression, Numerical Value, Multiple Choice, Equation, Open-Ended, Inequality
First Physics-Olympiad leaderboard — 13 physics Olympiads from 2024–2025 with official medal cutoffs
Direct human-model comparison — HiPhO benchmarks (M)LLM exam scores against human contestants
Medal cutoffs are derived from the theoretical exam scores of human medalists.
Only the theoretical components of each exam are evaluated; experimental and diagram-drawing problems are excluded, so Full Mark (Model) ≤ Full Mark (Human).
Each model was run 8 times. Problem scores were averaged and summed to compute the final exam score.
For Kimi-K2-Thinking, the inference timeout is set to 2 hours, and 9.58% of cases exceed this limit.
Models are ranked by the average score across all 13 Olympiad exams
the first benchmark dedicated to high school physics Olympiads with human-aligned evaluation
across 13 exams, open-source MLLMs mostly remain at or below the bronze level
closed-source reasoning MLLMs can achieve 6 to 12 gold medals
It compiles 13 latest Olympiad exams from 2024–2025, spanning both international and regional competitions
Submitted on 9 Sep 2025 ( v1 ), last revised 19 Sep 2025 (this version, v4)
Title: HiPhO: How Far Are (M)LLMs from Humans in the Latest High School Physics Olympiad Benchmark?
Total Problems 360
- Total Subquestions 519
Total Physics Fields 5
Total Modality Types 4
Total Answer Types 6
Total Difficulty Levels 3
Language (EN : ZH) 308:52
- With Medal Scorelines 13
- With Marking Schemes 7
includes 360 problems and 519 subquestions from 13 Olympiad-level exam papers held in 2024–2025
All problems are carefully verified by expert annotators to ensure accuracy.
covering five fields (Mechanics, Electromagnetism, Thermodynamics, Optics, and Modern Physics)
Beyond fine-grained scoring, we use exam score instead of accuracy to provide a more faithful measure of overall exam performance.

This enables direct comparison with actual student scores and official medal thresholds, providing the first quantitative analysis of the performance gap between state-of-the-art (M)LLMs and top human contestants in real-world physics competitions.
As shown in Fig. 3, expression is the most common (45%)
The next most frequent type is numerical values (27%)
Text-Only (TO): Problems are stated entirely in text with no figures.
Text+Illustration Figure (TI): Figures depict scenarios, while the text provides the description.
At the subquestion level, answers are classified into six types, including Expression, Numerical Value, Multiple Choice, Equation, Inequality, and Open-Ended.
Problems are labeled by five major fields—Mechanics, Electromagnetism, Thermodynamics, Optics, and Modern Physics.
We first apply rule-based math-verifier (Kydlı́ček) to determine whether the extracted model answer matches the ground truth.
Problem Score = max(answer-level score, step-level score)
The exam score is then obtained by summing the scores of all problems.
For problems with multiple official solutions (e.g., NBPhO), we score all marking schemes and take the highest result to ensure fairness across alternative solving paths.
Compared to GPT-4o, Gemini-2.5-Flash provides step-level scores more closely aligned with human experts, with under 1-point differences in the examples
Closed-source reasoning MLLMs collected 6–12 gold medals across the 13 exams
in IPhO-2025 the top human scored 29.2/30, while the best model achieved only 22.7/29.4
Open-source MLLMs mostly remained at or below the bronze threshold, with Intern-S1 the only exception to reach gold.
Open-source LLMs generally outperformed open-source MLLMs, earning gold in easier contests such as F=MA
in the challenging IPhO-2025, only three of them reached the gold threshold, with the top two separated by merely 0.4 points
Here, only the theoretical parts of exams are used, hence Full Mark (Model) ≤ Full Mark (Human).
Models are ranked by medal counts
In PanPhO-2025, its 60.3 points were far below the top human score of 81.
Kimi-K2-Instruct achieved 65.9 points compared to the top human score of 62.0
in PanPhO-2025 Intern-S1 scored above 40 points, surpassing the median performance of human medalists, yet still below the gold threshold
diagram-based problems are consistently more difficult than text-only ones
Mechanics and Electromagnetism show a clear source gap. Closed-source models average above 70%.
Since most models lack embodiment and generative capabilities, all experimental and diagram-generation problems are excluded to ensure fair evaluation.
physics Olympiads require not only interpreting diagrams but also sketching functional plots
As a result, the Full Mark (Model) in Table 3 may be lower than the Full Mark (Human).
IPhO, APhO, and EuPhO include separate experimental exams, and NBPhO integrates theoretical and experimental problems within a single paper.
Among the 13 exams, 7 provide official marking schemes, and 4 support multiple solutions.
we exclude all experimental and diagram-generation questions for fair and consistent evaluation
The Full Mark (Model) in Table 3 therefore refers only to the theoretical score of the theoretical exam.
Step-level scores are typically higher than answer-level scores in the final exam results, reflecting the partial credit awarded for intermediate steps.
each problem is tested using eight independent inference runs at a temperature of 0.6
We adopt VLMEvalKit (Duan et al., 2024) as the evaluation framework for benchmarking MLLMs.
we evaluate 30 representative models, including 11 closed-source MLLMs, 11 open-source MLLMs, and 8 open-source LLMs
